iut_type: End Product (Allied Telesis GEN2 device), Wireless Gecko Link Layer/Host AoA/AoD mismatch
customer_question: We'd like to register referencing this specific QDID combination (a Wireless Gecko Link Layer and Host based on Core Specification 5.4, plus our RF PHY QDID) — is the cost and test duration you previously quoted still accurate for this combination?
question_variants: Can this exact QDID combination be registered as proposed?
If not, is there an alternative within the same product family that works?
actual_issue: The customer proposed a specific Link Layer/Host QDID combined with their own RF PHY QDID, not realizing that the Link Layer QDID's AoA/AoD direction-finding capability didn't match their actual RF PHY's lack of AoA/AoD support, which would produce a fatal cross-layer inconsistency ineligible for a Test Case Waiver.
plain_english_explanation: The proposed Link Layer QDID supports AoA/AoD (direction-finding) functionality, but the customer's actual RF PHY QDID does not support AoA/AoD — this mismatch produces numerous cross-layer inconsistencies that fall outside what a Test Case Waiver can excuse, making this exact combination unregisterable. However, the same underlying 'Wireless Gecko Link Layer and Host based on Core Specification 5.4' registration has many pre-defined Subset DNs available — narrower-capability variants of the same base registration — including one that is both AoA/AoD-incapable and Class 1-incapable, matching the customer's actual RF PHY capability. Referencing this specific Subset DN instead of the full-capability QDID avoids the fatal inconsistency entirely and allows registration to proceed via Test Case Waiver, at the same previously-quoted cost.
consultant_answer: Your proposed Link Layer QDID supports AoA/AoD direction-finding, but your actual RF PHY QDID doesn't — this mismatch produces inconsistencies that a Test Case Waiver can't excuse, so this exact combination can't be registered as proposed. However, the same base registration ('Wireless Gecko Link Layer and Host based on Core Specification 5.4') has a Subset DN available that's both AoA/AoD-incapable and Class 1-incapable, matching your actual RF PHY capability — referencing that Subset DN instead avoids the inconsistency and lets registration proceed via Test Case Waiver, at the same cost we previously quoted.
decision_logic: When a proposed Link Layer/Host QDID claims a capability (like AoA/AoD) that the paired RF PHY QDID doesn't actually support, check whether the same base registration offers a narrower-capability Subset DN matching the actual RF PHY capability, rather than concluding the registration is blocked entirely.
final_recommendation: When a customer proposes a specific QDID combination, verify capability alignment between Link Layer/Host and RF PHY components (not just whether each individually exists), and proactively search for matching Subset DNs under the same base registration when a capability mismatch is found.
risk_if_done_wrong: Proceeding with the proposed full-capability QDID without checking for the AoA/AoD mismatch would produce a registration blocked by inconsistencies ineligible for TCW, forcing a costly do-over once discovered; failing to search for the matching Subset DN could lead to concluding the registration was impossible entirely.
